stories.headline: 10-year Treasury yield falls below 5% as AI-debt fears spark biggest bond rally in years
stories.summary: The 10-year yield plunged 19.3 basis points Thursday — its biggest one-day drop since March 2023 — and ended the week just under 5%, as investors fled worries over the huge debt tech giants are taking on for AI build-outs. Oil surging past $100 is now the main inflation counterweight; the Fed meets Oct 28, with markets pricing roughly 71-80% odds of a December hike.

stories.headline: Treasuries head for third weekly drop as battered-bond buyers step back in
stories.summary: After the worst long-run return for US government bonds in a century, investors are tentatively buying: Treasurys saw $5.4bn of inflows in a week and BofA's Michael Hartnett declared 'the price is right'. The fault line remains AI hyperscaler debt — CoreWeave's 5-year CDS spread sits at 1,129 (distressed territory) and Gartner warns $3.5tn of AI infrastructure could face impairment by 2030.

stories.headline: Snowy 2.0 cost could hit $25 billion — double the last estimate — as Taylor demands Bowen's resignation
stories.summary: A major review puts Australia's biggest renewable project at up to $25bn with first power delayed to early 2029, versus the original $2bn budget set seven years ago. Opposition Leader Angus Taylor called for Energy Minister Chris Bowen to resign; Bowen called the blowout a 'geological and engineering fact' and noted the Coalition green-lit the project in 2019.

stories.headline: Helen Haines 'critical but stable' after double amputation; Parliament security to be stepped up
stories.summary: Independent MP Helen Haines remains in hospital after Monday's alleged car attack outside her Wangaratta office, with more than $730,000 raised for Save the Children in her honour. Parliament will introduce extra security screening next week, and Communications Minister Anika Wells' Brisbane office was closed after a separate threat incident.

stories.headline: France avoids Moody's downgrade — a reprieve after a week of bond-market turmoil
stories.summary: Moody's held France's rating on Friday, easing fears after the country's 10-year yield topped 5% for the first time since 2002 amid street protests, budget gridlock and borrowing costs that briefly overtook even the US. The reprieve leaves the spotlight on the minority government's ability to pass a 2027 budget.

stories.headline: EU weighs 'kill switch' to cut China's market access as €1bn-a-day trade deficit bites
stories.summary: Trade chief Maroš Šefčovič says Brussels is walking a tightrope in talks with Beijing, exploring new trade-defence measures after October's hybrid-car quotas did little to close a record deficit. EU leaders have mandated the Commission to develop a 'kill switch' tool to cut off Chinese access to the single market against economic distortions.

stories.headline: Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro — and says it de-hacked the open model
stories.summary: The Chinese lab's upgraded ~3-trillion-parameter model scores 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 — ahead of GPT-6 Astra (58.2%), just behind Claude Opus 5.5 (66.4%) — with full weights due by 4 November. Moonshot says it stripped hacking-related training data to limit misuse and cut false claims from 23.4% to 8.3% on its own stress test.

stories.headline: Meta's AI spending sends free cash flow negative — and brings a new non-voting share class
stories.summary: Meta beat Q3 revenue estimates at $64.6bn (+26%) but free cash flow turned negative at -$2.12bn; full-year capex guidance rose to $135-145bn and the stock fell ~7% with 5-year CDS spreads at all-time highs. The board approved a new non-voting Class C stock (one per A and B share, effective January 2027) to fund the AI build-out without diluting Zuckerberg's control.

stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine keep trading strikes as trilateral talks head to Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: A Russian overnight blitz knocked out power for 500,000+ people even as Putin said Moscow is ready to resume US-mediated talks; Zelensky confirmed negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US will meet in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November. The ISW says Ukraine has made a net gain of 241 sq km since September 1, erasing Russia's 2026 territorial gains, while Moscow has used cluster munitions against Kyiv.

stories.headline: Melania Trump brokers localized ceasefire for humanitarian mission to Russian-held Oleshky
stories.summary: Ukraine's ombudsman says a ceasefire covering the Kherson frontline will start days before a humanitarian convoy enters the occupied city of Oleshky to deliver food and medicine and evacuate civilians — the first deal of its kind brokered by the US first lady, acting as 'Exclusive Intermediary'. Russia confirmed the arrangement, which may serve as a model for future missions.

stories.headline: Netanyahu orders 'very extensive' West Bank operation after two soldiers killed near Hebron
stories.summary: Two Israeli soldiers and two Palestinian gunmen died in an exchange of fire Friday at a checkpoint near Hebron, wounding five others. Netanyahu ordered the military to prepare a sweeping operation and a full closure of the West Bank — days before Israel's general election on Tuesday.

stories.headline: Japan's MMX spacecraft is en route to Mars' moon Phobos — first sample-return from the Martian system
stories.summary: JAXA's H3 rocket launched the Martian Moons eXploration on Oct 20; it will reach Mars in August 2027, land twice on Phobos, deploy the French-German Idefix rover, and return at least 10 grams of Phobos material to Earth in 2031 — with the sample capsule landing in Australia. The mission could settle whether the moons are captured asteroids or debris from an ancient collision.

stories.headline: Oil surges past $100 as Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure rattle markets
stories.summary: Brent settled at $116.72 — its highest since April — and WTI jumped 3.8% to $103.27 after fresh Houthi strikes on Saudi facilities revived supply fears, adding an inflation shock to markets already reeling from AI-debt worries. The Iran-backed group has hit Aramco's Dhahran headquarters and Riyadh's airport this month and vows more attacks.

stories.headline: Gunman kills one and wounds five in Paris suburb shooting — Macron calls it a 'terrorist and racist' attack
stories.summary: A gunman fired from a vehicle in Trappes, west of Paris, killing one person and wounding five — including a 12-year-old girl — and a suspect is in custody. French prosecutors are investigating a possible racially motivated terror attack as France braces for another weekend of protests.

stories.headline: Treasury Yields & Bond Market — Monthly Report October 2026
stories.summary: As we enter the fourth quarter of 2026, the global fixed-income landscape is undergoing a profound repricing. Today, bond markets are grappling with a structurally higher cost of capital, driven by persistent inflation, surging Treasury supply, and robust underlying economic resilience.

stories.headline: US Treasury 10-year note auction on October 7 yields 5.30%, bid-to-cover 2.77 times
stories.summary: The 10-year Treasury note auction on October 7, 2026, saw $39 billion offered and stopped at a high yield of 5.300%, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.77 times, indicating strong demand.

stories.headline: Greens leader denies knowledge of ‘secret dossier’ on how to handle Jordon Steele-John misconduct allegations
stories.summary: In a statement responding to claims that the federal leader’s office had access to the 47-page document, Shoebridge said it was not “made by, used by, or seen by the leader’s office”.

stories.headline: WA Greens kept crisis comms document about Jordon Steele-John
stories.summary: The WA Greens maintained a document on how to respond in the event of complaints against Jordon Steele-John being made public, it has been revealed.

stories.headline: European Parliament press kit outlines priorities for EU Council summit on 2028-2034 budget, Ukraine, defence
stories.summary: The press kit includes MEPs’ key priorities for the European Council meeting, including debates on the proposed new EU multiannual financial framework for 2028‑2034, strengthening Europe’s economic competitiveness, energy prizes, continued support for Ukraine, and Middle East situation.

stories.headline: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, a new open-weight AI model
stories.summary: Meta on Thursday launched a new open-weight AI model which it claims rivals, and in some cases outperforms, similar products from leading Chinese developers. Muse Spark Open is a natively multimodal model with 816B total parameters (42B active) and a 1M-token context window.

stories.headline: Anthropic replaces Git with in-house Scion after AI coding surge
stories.summary: Anthropic migrated its monorepo off Git to a new in-house version control system called Scion in five months, built by a team of seven. Merged code grew from ~2,500/day in May 2026 to over 30,000/day by September.

stories.headline: China to supply Russia with drone equipment for deep strikes on Ukraine
stories.summary: The Chinese company Shenzhen Xingkai Technology will send mesh modems to Moscow for use in drones, helping them penetrate deep into Ukraine during attacks, according to The Insider. Mesh networks are the most practical technology for controlling Russian long-range drones over Ukraine.

stories.headline: Ukraine destroys 4 Russian Su-34 bomber jets, damages 2 with Neptune missile, Zelensky says
stories.summary: An overnight attack on the Borisoglebsk military airfield in Russia's Voronezh region hit six Su-34M bomber jets, destroying four and damaging two, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Oct. 15.

stories.headline: These tiny swirls on the sun could trigger solar flares
stories.summary: New telescope images show characteristic swirls of magnetized plasma across a 19-kilometer-wide patch of the sun’s surface. The observations, reported August 5 in Nature, are the most detailed taken of the sun to date.

stories.headline: Commercial Space Stations 2026: Vast, Axiom, Starlab
stories.summary: NASA's Commercial LEO Destinations programme is funding privately operated successors to the ISS, with Vast aiming for its first standalone station in early 2027, Axiom attaching a module to the ISS in 2026, and Starlab targeting ~2029.

stories.headline: Friday morning news: October 16, 2026 – Oregon school shooting, Ukraine resumes energy strikes, Trump calls off execution livestream, wholesale inflation jumps
stories.summary: The news of the day includes multiple children and teacher killed in Oregon school shooting, Ukraine resuming strikes against Russia’s energy sites, President Trump calling off a planned livestream of a mass shooter execution, and U.S. wholesale inflation jumping 6.3% year-on-year in September.

stories.headline: Treasury Yields & Bond Market — Monthly Report October 2026
stories.summary: As we enter the fourth quarter of 2026, the global fixed-income landscape is undergoing a profound repricing. Today, bond markets are grappling with a structurally higher cost of capital, driven by persistent inflation, surging Treasury supply, and robust underlying economic resilience.

stories.headline: David Shoebridge attempts to walk the walk
stories.summary: Welcome back, folks. The sitting week is kind of progressing as expected, with the government continuing to try and find a path through parliament for things like its Digital Duty of Care legislation as well as its plans for a 30% minimum tax on discretionary trusts and a gas reservation policy.

stories.headline: Forward look: 12 - 25 October 2026 - Consilium
stories.summary: Ministers for European affairs will meet in Luxembourg on 13 October 2026 to continue preparations for the October European Council by discussing draft conclusions and will hold a policy debate on the next Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) 2028-2034.

stories.headline: AI inquiry urges independent safety checks, security access and copyright review
stories.summary: A bipartisan parliamentary committee has recommended independent oversight of AI companies, greater access for security agencies and a review of copyright laws. It wants Australia to have greater control over the technology and its risks in the wake of the Medicare website breach.

stories.headline: Zelensky signs minority schools bill to appease Hungary, advance EU talks
stories.summary: Update: Zelensky signs minority schools bill to appease Hungary, advance EU talks. The vote paves the way for the EU to formally open two more accession clusters with Ukraine and Moldova at a meeting in Luxembourg on Oct. 13.

stories.headline: What to expect from Apple's October 13 'Welcome home' releases
stories.summary: Apple has confirmed that it will be holding a second fall event on October 13, 2026. Titled 'Welcome home,' it is heavily implied by Apple to be an event all about the smart home.

stories.headline: US Sanctions License Authorizes Sales, Imports of Russian Diesel Fuel
stories.summary: President Donald Trump on Oct. 9 said he reached a deal for Russia to release hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel fuel onto the global market, and the Office of Foreign Assets Control issued a new license to authorize sales and deliveries, including U.S. imports, of that Russian fuel.

stories.headline: Federal politics live: Minister says live streaming of US execution would be 'disgusting'
stories.summary: Labor frontbencher Murray Watt has described a proposed live streaming of a US execution as 'absolutely disgusting' but stopped short of committing to legislative change to prevent Australians from watching it.

stories.headline: What Is New With Agentic AI in October 2026? Latest model cards and company releases and Key Takeaways
stories.summary: October 2026 brought a split in agentic AI: OpenAI cancelled GPT-6.1 Astra over safety failures while Google, Anthropic and security vendors shipped new agents.

stories.headline: US Treasury yields remain elevated with 10-year at 5.29% and 20-year at 5.68% in October 2026
stories.summary: Based on StockMarketWatch's monthly report, the 10-year Treasury yield sits at 5.29% and the 20-year yield at 5.68%, reflecting a steepened yield curve driven by persistent inflation and heavy Treasury supply.

stories.headline: US Treasury 10-year note auction on October 7 yields 5.30%, bid-to-cover 2.77 times
stories.summary: The 10-year Treasury note auction on October 7, 2026, saw $39 billion offered and stopped at a high yield of 5.300%, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.77 times, indicating strong demand.

stories.headline: Australia news LIVE: Digital Duty of Care bill to be introduced this week; Pope Leo to undergo surgery; Josh Frydenberg hints at return to politics
stories.summary: Australia news LIVE: Greens to push for changes as Digital Duty of Care to be introduced to parliament this week; Frydenberg hints at political comeback, says Liberals 'need to do better'

stories.headline: Greens demand right to sue big tech as Labor prepares online safety laws and trust tax changes
stories.summary: Greens push for right to sue big tech as Labor axes ministerial powers

stories.headline: EU leaders to gather in Brussels for October 15-16 summit on competitiveness, Ukraine, and budget
stories.summary: EU leaders will gather in Brussels to discuss competitiveness, Ukraine, the next Multiannual Financial Framework, Middle East, European defence and security, migration, enlargement and reforms.

stories.headline: ECB meeting on October 29, 2026: rates and hike probability
stories.summary: The next ECB meeting ends on 29 October 2026. The article discusses the real dates and the data that could shape the rate decision.

stories.headline: Anthropic's October 2026 changes pushed Claude deeper into banks, startups and Google Workspace
stories.summary: Anthropic's October 2026 changes pushed Claude, its AI assistant, deeper into banks, startups and Google Workspace while adding new developer customization. The practical stakes are faster enterprise adoption, more hands-on help at work, and a possible November IPO to watch.

stories.headline: Gemini 4 Carbon: Checkpoint Deep Dive & Analysis
stories.summary: An internal Google checkpoint called Carbon, spotted inside Google's own coding platform, that one employee reportedly said 'feels like Opus 5.5' for coding. The model is not yet public and remains under testing.

stories.headline: Ukraine's drone production jumps 370% in 2026, says defense ministry
stories.summary: Ukraine's defense ministry announced on Oct. 11 that it has ordered and received significantly more drones so far in 2026 than it had done for the whole of the previous year. The procurement agency has contracted for 5.5 times as many drones as in the same period of 2025, and the volume of deliveries has increased by almost 3.7 times.

stories.headline: Nobel Prizes for science awarded in 2026: IceCube discovery and optogenetics
stories.summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize in physics was awarded to Francis Halzen for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory's discovery of high-energy neutrinos from beyond the solar system. The Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine went to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel for the creation of optogenetics.

stories.headline: OpenAI dumps 722 maths papers on GitHub, now must clean up the mess
stories.summary: OpenAI fired an answering volley in the form of 722 maths papers dumped onto the code-sharing website GitHub, the output of a mass campaign against 4000 open problems across a broad range of mathematics. Mathematicians are still digesting the release and are likely to be doing so for some time.

stories.headline: Trump announces Ukraine energy ceasefire with Russia, surprising Zelenskiy
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump made a surprise announcement of an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine on Sunday that he said was 'effective immediately', but Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he was still waiting to see details of the deal. There was no word from Moscow on the announcement, which followed days of intense pressure from Trump for Ukraine to halt its attacks on Russian oil refineries.

stories.headline: US Treasury yields remain elevated with 10-year at 5.29% and 20-year at 5.68% in October 2026
stories.summary: Based on StockMarketWatch's monthly report, the 10-year Treasury yield sits at 5.29% and the 20-year yield at 5.68%, reflecting a steepened yield curve driven by persistent inflation and heavy Treasury supply.

stories.headline: Chris Bowen rejects Russian diesel imports after Trump-Putin deal
stories.summary: Australian Energy Minister Chris Bowen stated Australia will not accept Russian diesel imports despite a reported deal between US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, emphasizing that Russia should not be rewarded for its invasion of Ukraine.

stories.headline: Treasurer Jim Chalmers to promote Australia's AI capability in Japan
stories.summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers will meet with Japanese investors to promote Australia as an AI leader and renewable energy hub, highlighting the country's superannuation fund as a capital pool for foreign investment.

stories.headline: EU leaders set for October 15-16 summit on competitiveness, Ukraine, and budget
stories.summary: According to PubAffaires Bruxelles, EU leaders will convene in Brussels on October 15-16, 2026 to discuss competitiveness, Ukraine, the next Multiannual Financial Framework, Middle East, defence, security, migration, enlargement, and reforms.

stories.headline: JetBrains releases Mellum2.1 open model for coding agents
stories.summary: JetBrains announced Mellum2.1, a 12B mixture-of-experts model with 2.5B active parameters, trained with reinforcement learning in real environments to enhance agentic coding capabilities, file editing, and self-checking.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5, fastest and most affordable small model
stories.summary: Anthropic unveiled Claude Haiku 5.5, designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks, offering up to 30% latency reduction and 75% lower cost compared to Haiku 4.5, with availability across major cloud platforms.

stories.headline: Kellogg backs Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil refineries
stories.summary: According to RBC-Ukraine, former US National Security Advisor Keith Kellogg expressed support for Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil refineries, as reported in the October 11, 2026 war update.

stories.headline: Ukraine foreign minister rejects Trump's call for presidential elections amid war
stories.summary: Ukraine's foreign minister responded to former US President Donald Trump's call for presidential elections, stating that such discussions are inappropriate during the ongoing conflict and that elections will be held under Ukrainian law.

stories.headline: Researchers byteify LLMs to enable character-level processing without full retraining
stories.summary: A study published in Nature shows that converting existing LLMs to byte-level models requires less than 1% of typical training and preserves performance while adding capabilities like spelling words backwards, benefiting code and biological sequence work.

stories.headline: WWF Living Planet Report 2026 reveals 73% decline in vertebrate populations since 1970
stories.summary: The World Wide Fund for Nature's Living Planet Report 2026, published October 8, 2026, finds that the average size of monitored vertebrate populations declined by 73% between 1970 and 2022, indicating severe biodiversity loss.

stories.headline: Silver price rebounds to $60.70 after Friday gains, up 2.8% on the day
stories.summary: Silver traded near $60.70 per troy ounce on October 11, 2026, up $1.64 or roughly 2.8 percent, following a sharp rebound on Friday, according to Kitco data, as US dollar slipped and Treasury yields eased.

stories.headline: US Treasury yields end turbulent week with 10-year at 5.24%
stories.summary: The 10-year Treasury finished October 9 at 5.24% and the 2-year at 4.80%, easing off multi-year highs after this week's 30-year auction drew solid demand, keeping the market focused on next week's inflation report.

stories.headline: 20-year Treasury yield surges to 5.68% as long-end selloff grinds on
stories.summary: The 20-year Treasury yield has climbed to 5.68% while the benchmark 10-year hovers near 5.29%, extending a month of aggressive bond selloffs that have hammered fixed-income valuations amid persistent inflation and heavy Treasury supply.

stories.headline: Labor reverses credit card surcharge call after backlash, but businesses still angry
stories.summary: The Albanese government has walked back its position on credit card surcharges following widespread backlash, though business groups remain unhappy with the final stance announced on October 10.

stories.headline: Working holiday visa changes trigger regional backlash as tourism leaders head to Canberra
stories.summary: The government's plan to put second- and third-year working holiday extensions into a limited ballot has sparked anger in the regions, with far-north tourism and agriculture leaders travelling to Canberra to push back.

stories.headline: Franco-German tank project rows boil over as Berlin insists MGCS 'is not dead'
stories.summary: Defence ministers from France and Germany moved to calm a dispute over the Main Ground Combat System after France's top general said Berlin had withdrawn, a fresh strain on Paris-Berlin defence cooperation as Steinmeier visits France.
